text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

PALM OIL SALE - State-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan bought 4,000 tonnes of palm olein for shipment by December 20 at its tender on Tuesday, European vegetable oil traders said. The TCP bought from the lowest bidder Qulei Edible Oil of Malaysia at $577.93 a tonne c and f.

SOY AND CORN TENDER - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on Wednesday for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow soybeans for December arrival.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd has invited tenders for 22,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Wednesday, traders said. Shipment was set for February 1-28 to the western port of Inchon.
- The CCC was tendering on November 20 for up to 16,910 tonnes of U.S. number two hard red winter wheat for export to Mozambique. Shipment was slated for Dec 5-31.

- The CCC said it was tendering on November 20 for up to 16,100 tonnes of U.S. wheat for export to Iraq. Shipment was slated for December 5-30. It sought number two or better wheat, excluding unclassed, mixed and durum wheat.

CORN TENDER - South Africa's Western Cape Buyers Association said on Monday it planned to import 250,000 tonnes of yellow maize this season and next. Due to a shortage of yellow corn this season, caused by excessive exports, the group said it had decided to invite tenders for the delivery of 30,000 tonnes of maize in February, 40,000 in March and 60,000 in April. The April consignment has been contracted.
SOYMEAL TENDER - South Korea's Korea Feed Association passed on tenders for a total of 70,000 tonnes due to high prices.

RICE TENDER - Jamaica is tendering on November 18 for 2,500 tonnes of U.S. bulk brown rice under the GSM-102 program, agents for the buyer said. The rice can be offered FOB U.S. Gulf for December 1-20 delivery or cost and freight Montego Bay, December 21-27. Results are due Wednesday.

MARKET TALK - India's grain procurement agency said on Tuesday that it will release an additional 100,000 tonnes of wheat for domestic sales in November to check rising prices. The Food Corporation of India said the fresh allotment of 100,000 tonnes would raise the total amount of wheat to be released this month to 499,000 tonnes.

... The Egyptian state's General Authority for Supply Commodities said on Tuesday that 105,000 tonnes of French wheat had been cleared at Port Said despite an unusually high proportion of foreign matter.
...Turkey may import an unspecified amount of wheat to control bread prices after the Argentine grain crop comes on to the market next month, Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said on Tuesday.

Bread prices have risen 30 percent in the past three weeks. "(The) grain harvest in Argentina...will begin next month and, if need be, wheat will then be imported and bread prices will be adjusted," he told parliament.
